facts.fact: The CNDP deliberation of 23 April 2020 treats payment institutions (établissements de paiement) as a category operating remote account opening alongside banks, and permits both to use facial recognition for it on prior authorisation; it names no payment law.

note: Names no payments law or rule; only the existence of payment institutions beside banks.

facts.fact: Le Matin, reporting the 11th MFC Talks, says Morocco has a regulatory framework already well advanced, and that a first phase led by Bank Al-Maghrib laid the regulatory bases, organised interoperability and governed access to infrastructures; no law or rule is named.

Le Matin reports payment institutions (établissements de paiement) and fintechs taking part with banks in Morocco's payments market, with licensed players carrying regulation and compliance for fintechs; no licensing rule is named.
CMI says its Fatourati platform is interconnected to 32 banks and payment institutions (établissements de paiement) as at February 2026; no law or rule is named.

systems.tiers: 32 banks and payment institutions; fintechs and invoicing-software publishers via Fatourati Agrégateur

facts.fact: Bank Al-Maghrib decision n° 265/W/2026 of 6 July 2026 cut the cap on domestic card interchange fees from 0.65% (set October 2024) to 0.50%, effective 1 October 2026, and BAM supervises payment establishments against its security, continuity and reliability requirements for payment services; the joint communiqué names no payments law and gives its own date 2026-07-10.

Bank Al-Maghrib and the Competition Council state that newly licensed payment establishments (établissements de paiement) and already licensed ones are deploying card-acquiring activity in Morocco, with BAM overseeing them; the communiqué is dated 2026-07-10 and gives no licensing dates.

facts.fact: Law 103-12 on credit institutions, enacted by Dahir 1-14-193 of 24 December 2014 and given here as amended, defines payment means including electronic money (Article 6) and payment services (Article 16), and regulates payment institutions (Articles 15-18) as binding law.

facts.fact: Law 103-12 (2014) defines payment institutions (établissements de paiement) as entities offering payment services, separate from credit institutions, and requires them to obtain Bank Al-Maghrib approval before operating in Morocco (Article 34).
